userStories.title: Persist one-shot dispatch usage
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Feed completed one-shot dispatches into the usage sidecar without changing stream-beat rows.

**Motivation** — A one-shot `complete()` dispatch emits no `agent.usage_update`, so today it writes a cost-ledger row and zero usage rows.

**Approach** — `attachUsageAuditSubscriber` additionally subscribes to `dispatchEvents.onDispatch` and records one row per `kind === "complete"` event: `input`/`output`/`cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` from `tokenUsage` (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadInputTokens`, `cacheCreationInputTokens`), `costUsd = exactCostUsd ?? estimatedCostUsd`, `cadence: "one-shot"`, `ts` from the event's `timestamp`, `scopeId`/`sessionName`/`storyId`/`stage`/`agentName` copied from the event, and `streamCallId` set to the event's `callId`, or the literal `"one-shot"` when the event has none. The returned function detaches both subscriptions. The single production caller is `src/runtime/index.ts:425`. A one-shot `complete` event with no `tokenUsage` and cost 0 writes no usage row, matching the cost subscriber which also skips it. Widen `UsageAuditEntry.cadence` to `"round-trip" | "agent" | "one-shot"`; insert `DispatchEventBus` into every existing test call and preserve their stream assertions. Test via `createRuntime` and `runtime.dispatchEvents` as well as a directly subscribed bus.

**Scope** — In: one-shot usage subscriber, entry union, production caller and existing test call sites. Out: in-flight residual tracking and partial cost rows (US-003/005), tool-audit sinks (US-004), changing the usage-audit default.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function attachUsageAuditSubscriber(bus: IAgentStreamEventBus, dispatchEvents: IDispatchEventBus, auditor: IUsageAuditor, runId: string): () => void;
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given attachUsageAuditSubscriber(bus, dispatchEvents, auditor, "run-1"), when a `complete` dispatch with tokenUsage {inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 20, cacheReadInputTokens: 5, cacheCreationInputTokens: 1} and exactCostUsd: 0.01 is emitted, then exactly one UsageAuditEntry is recorded with input: 100, output: 20, cacheRead: 5, cacheWrite: 1, costUsd: 0.01 and cadence: "one-shot".
When a `complete` event has exactCostUsd absent and estimatedCostUsd: 0.02, then its usage row has costUsd: 0.02.
When a `complete` event carries scopeId, sessionName, storyId, stage, agentName and callId, then its usage row copies those fields and sets streamCallId to callId.
When a `complete` event has no callId, then its usage row has streamCallId: "one-shot".
When a `session-turn` dispatch event is emitted, then it records no usage row.
When a `complete` event has no tokenUsage and cost 0, then it records no usage row.
When the function returned by attachUsageAuditSubscriber is called, then a later `complete` dispatch event and a later `agent.usage_update` event each record nothing.

Given a createRuntime runtime with agent.usageAudit.enabled: true, when a `complete` event is emitted on runtime.dispatchEvents and close() is called, then usage/<runId>.jsonl contains one row with cadence: "one-shot".

routing.reasoning: A simple second event-bus subscription changes the function signature and one runtime call site, with existing stream-beat behavior protected by tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: its calls to `attachUsageAuditSubscriber` pass three arguments `(bus, auditor, runId)`; the target signature inserts `dispatchEvents` as the second parameter. The replacing invariant: every existing call passes a `DispatchEventBus` as the second argument and its existing stream-event assertions are unchanged.

line 293 calls `attachUsageAuditSubscriber(bus, auditor, "r-001")` with three arguments; the target signature inserts `dispatchEvents` as the second parameter. The replacing invariant: the call passes a `DispatchEventBus` as the second argument and the test's assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: Track in-flight native spend and define partial cost rows
acceptanceCriteria: Given two agent.usage_update events with cadence: "round-trip" and roundTrip fields on stream callId c1, costs 0.10 and 0.15, and no agent.call_ended, when residuals() runs, then it returns one c1 entry with costUsd 0.25 and roundTrips 2.
Given two beats on c1 with inputTokens 10 and 30, one of which omits cacheRead, when residuals() runs, then its tokens.input is 40 and the absent cacheRead contributes 0 to tokens.cacheRead.
When agent.call_started carries model "m1" on c1, then its residual has model "m1"; a stream without call_started or with model "" has model "unknown".
When c1 receives agent.call_ended with status "success", then residuals() omits c1.
When c1 receives agent.call_ended with status "timeout", then residuals() omits c1.
When c1 receives agent.call_ended with status "cancelled", then residuals() retains c1.
Given cancelled c1 in sessionName n1, when a session-turn dispatch event has sessionName n1, then residuals() omits c1.
Given c1 in sessionName n1 ended with "error" and c2 in n1 ended with "success", when a session-turn dispatch event has sessionName n1, then residuals() retains c1.
Given two beats on c1 where only the first has a roundTrip field, when residuals() runs, then its roundTrips is 1.
Given c1 with scopeId s1 ended with "error", when a DispatchErrorEvent with scopeId s1 and tokenUsage is emitted, then residuals() omits c1.
Given c1 then c2, both with scopeId s1, ended with "error" in that order, when one DispatchErrorEvent with scopeId s1 and tokenUsage is emitted, then residuals() omits c2 and retains c1.
Given errored c1 with scopeId s1, when a DispatchErrorEvent has callId s1, no scopeId, and exactCostUsd 0.05, then residuals() omits c1.
Given errored c1 with scopeId s1, when a DispatchErrorEvent has scopeId s1, no tokenUsage and zero cost, then residuals() retains c1.
Given still-open c1 with scopeId s1, when a DispatchErrorEvent has scopeId s1 and tokenUsage, then residuals() retains c1.
When agent.usage_update events have cadence: "agent", then residuals() returns no entry for them.
Given a stream whose only beats have cost 0 and zero tokens, when residuals() runs, then it omits that stream.

When toPartialCostEvent maps a residual with sessionName "feat-US-001-acceptance-gen", then the CostEvent has partial: true, schemaVersion: 7, sessionRole: "acceptance-gen", costUsd, estimatedCostUsd and exactCostUsd equal to residual.costUsd, confidence: "estimated", roundTripUnit: "model-call", callId equal to streamCallId, and no pricingSource.
Given a residual whose sessionName maps to no known role, when toPartialCostEvent runs, then its CostEvent has no sessionRole field.
COST_ROW_SCHEMA_VERSION is 7, and a successful session-turn dispatch recorded by attachCostSubscriber has no partial field.

routing.reasoning: New two-bus per-stream lifecycle and newest-ended matching rules need isolated behavioral tests before implementation; the cost schema edit is small but the state machine is not.

modifiedFiles.reason: lines 588-589, 701 and 714 pin `schemaVersion` and `COST_ROW_SCHEMA_VERSION` to the literal `6`. The replacing invariant: they pin `7`, the version that adds `partial`.

lines 133-134, 146, 638-639 and 651 pin `schemaVersion` and `COST_ROW_SCHEMA_VERSION` to the literal `6`, and the comments at lines 8 and 470 name version 6. The replacing invariant: they pin and name `7`.

userStories.title: Flush open tool-audit buffers as partial at close
acceptanceCriteria: Given an unflushed createToolAuditSink sink with header.runId "r1" and one recorded call, when flushOpenToolAuditSinks("r1") runs, then one file is written whose body has partial: true and contains that call.
Given flushOpenToolAuditSinks("r1") ran, when that sink's own flush() runs, then no second file is written.
Given a sink's own flush() already ran, when flushOpenToolAuditSinks("r1") runs later, then it is not written again.
Given a sink has no recorded calls, when flushOpenToolAuditSinks("r1") runs, then no file is written for it.
When flushOpenToolAuditSinks("r1") runs, then it does not flush a sink registered under runId "r2".
When a sink's normal flush() writes a body, then it has no partial field.

Given one registered sink's write rejects, when flushOpenToolAuditSinks runs, then it writes the other sinks for that runId, logs a warning with message "tool-audit partial flush failed", and resolves.
When flushOpenToolAuditSinks is imported from the `@/tools` barrel and invoked, then it flushes a sink registered through createToolAuditSink.
Given a sink created without header.runId, when flushOpenToolAuditSinks runs for any runId, then it writes nothing for that sink.

Given a createRuntime runtime and a createToolAuditSink sink with header.runId matching runtime.runId and one recorded call, when runtime.close() runs, then one tool-audit file with partial: true is written into the sink's directory.

routing.reasoning: A new per-run registry coordinates asynchronous sink writes, terminal flush semantics and error isolation across the tools and runtime modules.

userStories.title: Record in-flight residual spend as partial cost rows at close
acceptanceCriteria: Given a createRuntime runtime with agent.usageAudit.enabled: false, when agent.call_started and two cadence: "round-trip" agent.usage_update events costing 0.4 and 0.6 are emitted on runtime.agentStreamEvents and close() runs, then cost/<runId>.jsonl contains exactly one row with partial: true and costUsd: 1.0.
Given the same setup, when close() completes, then totalSpendUsd(runtime.costAggregator.snapshot()) includes the 1.0 partial spend.
Given an in-flight stream received agent.call_ended with status "success" before close(), when close() runs, then cost/<runId>.jsonl is absent or has no row with partial: true.
Given a runtime already closed after recording a partial row, when close() is called a second time, then no further partial row is added.

routing.reasoning: The tracker and sink registry are already implemented by prerequisites; this story only wires a subscriber and orders cost recording before the existing close drain in one runtime file.

analysis: Existing TypeScript repo, not greenfield. The advisory raw Bash screen checks lexical config paths before resolver-based PRD/queue matches (src/tools/policy-bash-raw.ts:78-122) and denies both named tokens and redirect targets with identical misleading write-only wording (:130-151); preserving the same two-pass match and all allow/deny outcomes is critical. src/tools/nax-owned-writes.ts:34-48 lexically identifies config, :67-85 identifies PRDs/root queue files, and :101-125 supplies the existing Write/Edit refusal with a path-exact planner exemption; expose a shared kind predicate without changing those semantics. src/prompts/sections/nax-artifacts.ts:21-43 and src/prompts/sections/scratchpad.ts:27-43 are emitted in modes beyond raw Bash; the latter derives its dir from src/tools/scratchpad.ts:25, whose Write description is at :39. Regenerate only added text in the three specified snapshots; existing test/unit/tools/policy-bash-raw.test.ts protects decisions. One-shot dispatch metadata and usage are in src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts:15-114; src/runtime/middleware/usage-audit.ts:1-43 currently consumes stream usage only, with persisted row shape in src/runtime/usage-auditor.ts:20-48 and a single production caller at src/runtime/index.ts:425. All calls in test/unit/runtime/middleware/usage-audit.test.ts:69-138 and test/unit/runtime/middleware/agent-stream-logging.test.ts:293 require the new bus argument; existing stream-beat assertions must stay unchanged. The cost subscriber's complete/no-usage-and-zero-cost skip is at src/runtime/middleware/cost.ts:120-135. Native stream callId is per turn whereas scopeId joins to the ledger (src/runtime/agent-stream-events.ts:9-35); cadence, optional roundTrip and end status are at :49-108. A DispatchErrorEvent has no sessionName and may identify scope by scopeId or callId (src/runtime/dispatch-events.ts:139-183). Track additive native round-trip deltas in memory without reading the usage sidecar, clear resolved success/timeout and watchdog-cancelled turns that dispatch, and only reconcile the newest ended-unrecorded scope match when dispatch-error reports spend. ACP agent-cadence values cannot be safely accumulated. CostEvent is defined in src/runtime/cost-aggregator.ts:3-145, which is 597 lines under a 600-line source gate; add the optional field compactly and document/bump v6 to v7 in src/runtime/middleware/cost.ts:20-95. Derive role with src/runtime/usage-auditor.ts:81-88. CostAggregator.record and drain persist partials and snapshot feeds totals, so src/execution/runner.ts:257-262 needs no change. Tool sinks buffer calls until flush (src/tools/tool-audit.ts:163-197); register those with header.runId when constructed, mark registry flush terminal, and preserve normal flush bodies. Expose the registry flush through src/tools/index.ts:1-74, not a deep import. Do not edit near-size-gate src/agents/coding-tool-support.ts, src/operations/build-hop-callback.ts or src/runtime/session-run-hop.ts. Runtime subscriptions and idempotent close are at src/runtime/index.ts:418-430 and :487-522; integrate tracker and tool flush without changing its existing allSettled set. New unit tests: test/unit/runtime/in-flight-usage.test.ts, test/unit/tools/tool-audit-registry.test.ts. Put runtime-close integration in new test/unit/runtime/runtime-close-partial.test.ts rather than test/unit/runtime/runtime.test.ts (611 lines) or test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.test.ts (772 lines) near the 800-line test gate. Existing tests test/unit/runtime/middleware/cost.test.ts and cost-rate-provenance.test.ts pin version 6 and need 7; normal tool-audit behavior is already in test/unit/tools/tool-audit.test.ts. Older persisted cost rows require no migration: partial is optional and absent on ordinary rows. US-001, US-002, US-003 and US-004 are independent; US-005 depends on US-002/003/004 because they supply adjacent production wiring, the tracker API and the tool registry.
outOfScope: Changing which commands the raw Bash screen allows or denies. Only the refusal text changes; every allow/deny decision stays identical.
Changing the gated-mode Bash policy, the sandbox writable roots, or path containment for `/tmp`. nax#2228 is a prompt-only fix.

Excluding `.nax/scratchpad/` from any quality gate. In this repository `lint:biome` covers only `src/ bin/ test/ scripts/` and tsc includes only `src` and `bin`, so a probe script there is not linted; repositories whose lint covers every file may lint it.

Partial cost rows for ACP turns. ACP `agent.usage_update` beats may carry running totals rather than per-beat deltas, and that semantics is unverified; the in-flight tracker ignores `cadence: "agent"` beats.
Writing an `exit-summary` line on the SIGINT path. None is written there today; `run.complete` and status.json carry the total.
Bumping `TOOL_AUDIT_SCHEMA_VERSION`. The `partial` field is additive and optional.

Changing `src/agents/coding-tool-support.ts`, `src/runtime/session-run-hop.ts` or `src/operations/build-hop-callback.ts`. Tool-audit sinks register themselves inside `createToolAuditSink`, so no sink needs to be threaded through these files, and two of them sit at 596-598 lines against the 600-line gate.
US-004 only: tool-audit sinks whose header `runId` differs from the runtime's own `runId` (a hop given a foreign `runId`, `session-run-hop.ts:32`) are not flushed by that runtime's `close()`.
Reconciling the residual difference between the usage sidecar and the cost ledger on a completed run beyond what one-shot rows and partial rows close.

US-003 only: turns whose stream events carry no `scopeId` and end with `error`/`cancelled` while a dispatch-error row also records their spend may be counted twice (once on the error row, once as partial). Only native protocol-fault errors carry spend, and native beats carry a `scopeId` whenever the op has one. Likewise, a one-shot `completeAs` error row sharing a `scopeId` with an ended session turn may clear that turn's entry.
